name: Carlos Khan

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the independent Work Futures Panel. What you say is confidential. What is an ordinary day at your firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I start by clearing the tax return questions the juniors left overnight, then check figures against client invoices. I like finding the odd number that saves a client an argument later, but the last hour is often spent proving how I spent the first seven. I am 43, a senior accountant with a master’s degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I use AI tools every day without letting them sign anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: All right, I can picture a small change rather than a new profession. At our firm the software already fills boxes, and I still have to ask where the number came from.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team that faster first drafts leave us more time with the awkward tax questions. I would still put my name only on work I have checked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I like having the tool in my day, but it has never paid our mortgage for me. My partner Leena works hospital shifts, and three months of expenses is our whole reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing returns and run the daily AI check on duplicate invoices, with source documents beside it. I would also send the corrected-file counts to my manager Nisha each month so she can see why review time matters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel fairly steady about my place in the team, though the mortgage makes me watch the monthly figures. A bad quarter at the firm would still matter even without a breakthrough.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened the last time the tool saved time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a bakery client had an invoice entered twice; the tool flagged it and I checked the original. The baker cared that I could explain the correction, not that a machine found it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would you show that work to?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nisha is my manager and she signs the staffing plan. I would show her the bakery correction alongside the hours saved, because my review work is worth showing while pay stays ordinary.

say: I would **check** every AI flagged figure against the client record before signing a return.
I would tell my team that **review time** still earns its place at the firm.
think: I can handle **small automation**, but our mortgage and three month reserve still need ordinary wages.
I want Nisha to see the **corrections**, not only a shorter timesheet.
do: Keep preparing **tax returns** and checking AI flags against original invoices.
Send Nisha **monthly correction counts** while my present paid caseload continues.
feel: **Steady** about work, with a watchful eye on the mortgage.
S0.quote: The baker cared that I could explain the correction, not that a machine found it.
fieldNote: Carlos treats the **AI tool** as an assistant to signed judgment; one duplicated bakery invoice makes his point.
His public confidence sits beside a **three month reserve** and mortgage, so routine work needs visible value to management.

steps.text: Keep preparing signed returns with daily AI flags checked against original invoices
Send Nisha monthly corrected file counts while paid work continues

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That sounds closer to the queue I see each morning. Fewer people may be needed to type and check the first version of an account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say to clients that we can turn routine returns around sooner while a chartered accountant still checks the unusual ones. I would not promise their fees will fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think Nisha may decide the next vacant junior desk does not need filling. My senior review work is stronger, but typical pay and three months saved are no shield if the whole caseload thins.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Nisha for paid time to learn the new firm-approved AI review tool on ten closed files, recording its errors and checking client privacy. If she refuses, I will keep doing assigned paid returns and note errors by hand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious rather than excited, even though I know the tool. It is my own hours I am measuring against software now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you make the test safe for clients?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten closed files have no live client consequence, and I can compare the tax schedules line by line. I would use the tool on live files only after Nisha signs a passing error and privacy report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your hours are cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Leena could take an extra hospital shift for one month, but I do not want our budget built on her exhaustion. If my hours actually fall, I will ask for a posted senior tax review role elsewhere with written pay and a start date before resigning. There are some similar accounting jobs nearby, though I would not bank on a vacancy.

say: I would tell clients **routine returns** may move faster, while a chartered accountant checks exceptions.
I would not promise **lower fees** before our firm sets them.
think: An unfilled **junior desk** could signal fewer paid hours for everyone later.
Three months of **savings** would go quickly against our mortgage.
do: Learn the **new review tool** on ten closed files in Nisha-approved paid time; use live only after signed error and privacy clearance.
If hours fall, seek a **posted senior role** with written pay and start date before resigning.
Keep **assigned paid returns** if Nisha refuses the test while the firm still offers them.
feel: **Anxious** about my own hours despite using AI every day.
S1.quote: My senior review work is stronger, but typical pay and three months saved are no shield if the whole caseload thins.
fieldNote: He moves early with an **approved test** because confidentiality and error counts matter more than speed claims.
He keeps **paid files** if testing is refused; a new job requires reduced hours and a written offer.

steps.text: Learn new review tool on ten closed files in Nisha-approved paid time
Adopt for live files only after Nisha signs passing error and privacy report
Keep assigned paid returns if Nisha refuses, only while firm offers them
If hours fall, seek posted senior role with written pay and start before resigning

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028, most of a tax return is thinking work, not lifting a box, so the later robots would not buy our office much time. I would tell colleagues to get clear facts about staffing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say publicly that clients still need someone accountable for disputed figures. I would ask the firm for its actual plan instead of talking about the end of accounting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect our accounts team would lose a large share of paid work in the first year after AGI. My partner Leena and I could cover only three months before the mortgage became a problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would cancel the second car lease at its renewal and put the released monthly payment into the reserve. If I am laid off after AGI arrives, I will apply for posted compliance jobs with written pay covering the mortgage and a confirmed start; until then I keep paid client files while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be awake at night over losing our income that quickly. It is an alarmed feeling, though I can still do the next sensible thing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which cost can you actually change now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The lease ends in February, so there is a real date for that decision. I would tell Leena before the renewal notice, because the second car helps with school pickup but bus days are possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make another job real enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not accept a vague promise of future compliance work. A posted vacancy and written pay that covers the mortgage have to come before I leave a paid seat, if I still have one.

say: I would ask the firm for **staffing facts** because desk accounts work faces AGI in 2028.
I would say clients still deserve **accountability** for disputed numbers.
think: I expect a **large fall** in my team’s paid work within the first AGI year.
Our **three month reserve** cannot carry the mortgage through a long gap.
do: Cancel our **second car lease** at renewal and save the released payment.
After job loss, apply for **posted compliance work** only with written mortgage covering pay and confirmed start.
Keep **paid client files** only while the firm still assigns them before any layoff.
feel: **Alarmed** about a likely abrupt income loss and mortgage pressure.
S2.quote: My partner Leena and I could cover only three months before the mortgage became a problem.
fieldNote: Desk analysis faces **2028 AGI** itself; later robots offer his accounts work no grace period.
The **car lease** releases new cash; a compliance move still needs an actual vacancy and adequate wages.

steps.text: Cancel second car lease at February renewal
Transfer released car payment into mortgage reserve
Keep paid client files only while the firm offers them
After layoff, seek posted compliance job with written mortgage covering pay and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years before AGI reaches the desk in 2031 gives me room to prepare, even though the eventual software may do nearly every check. The robots in 2034 are not the date an accountant waits for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team we can use the next five years to build a clear record of the client disputes we resolve. I would not call it job security.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think paid judgment on tax disputes might last longer than producing standard returns, but I cannot bank the mortgage on that guess. Leena’s shifts are steady now, and I want our reserve closer to six months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Nisha to fund a chartered tax dispute course and give me paid study time; if approved, I will enrol and complete its case exercises this year. If refused, I will work through free published decisions after the children sleep while keeping my assigned paid returns as long as they exist. In the first year after 2031, I would keep paid dispute files only while the firm assigns them and use our reserve if they stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious but less cornered than in the 2028 picture. Five years lets me learn tax-dispute work and build cash without pretending my accounting wage is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What amount could you set aside?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One hundred from my salary can go into the reserve each month if the mortgage and school costs stay where they are. I would set the transfer after payday, not count Leena’s overtime before she earns it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm will not pay for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If Nisha pays for the course, the fees and study hours are the gate. If not, the free decisions still teach me how an appeal is argued, though they are no qualification.

say: I would tell my team that **five years** before 2031 gives us time to document disputed tax work.
I would not sell that record as **job security**.
think: Tax dispute judgment may last, but I cannot pledge the **mortgage** against a guess.
I want closer to **six months** of reserve before desk work changes.
do: Enrol in the **tax dispute course** if Nisha funds fees and paid study time; otherwise study free decisions.
Transfer **100 monthly** from my salary if mortgage and school costs permit.
Keep **paid dispute files** only while assigned after 2031, using our reserve if paid work stops.
feel: **Anxious**, with enough time to act deliberately.
S3.quote: Five years lets me learn tax-dispute work and build cash without pretending my accounting wage is safe.
fieldNote: He treats **2031** as time for formal learning and new saving, without assuming professional judgment survives AGI.
Funded **fees and paid time** enable the course; free decisions and assigned paid returns are the fallback.

steps.text: Enrol in funded tax dispute course during paid study time if Nisha agrees
Study free decisions if unfunded; retain offered paid files, use reserve when work ends
Transfer 100 monthly from salary if mortgage and school costs allow

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 is a long stretch of school terms for our children. Accounts will still be desk work when AGI comes, so I will not treat 2039 robots as my deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say at work that we owe clients careful records for every year we still serve them. I would ask for a real succession plan for staff rather than a cheerful slogan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could be managing the team well in 2035 and still see paid contracts shrink after 2036. The longer runway matters because I can pay down some mortgage debt before that first year arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my signed returns while the firm still pays for them and send an extra 75 from ordinary salary against mortgage principal each month if school costs allow. After 2036, if contracts shrink, I would apply for an advertised client compliance role only when written pay, hours and start date fit the mortgage and school pickups.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now, with a plan that could be revised each year. I would be anxious if the firm actually cut contracts after 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much debt would you pay down now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra payment would be 75, not the whole household buffer. Leena and I would revisit it each September when the school bills arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our younger child will be finishing school near then, but I will not ask either child to plan a life around my uncertain job. I can give them honest figures when the time comes.

say: I would ask for a **staff plan** while we still prepare paid client accounts.
I would set **2036** as the desk deadline, not the later robot date.
think: Good team management may not protect my **contracts** after AGI.
A decade gives us time to reduce the **mortgage** without draining the reserve.
do: Pay an extra **75 monthly** against mortgage principal if school bills allow, reviewing each September.
After 2036 contraction, seek an **advertised compliance role** with written pay, hours and start date that fit our household.
Keep preparing **signed paid returns** only while the firm still assigns them.
feel: **Uneasy** now; anxious if paid contracts shrink later.
S4.quote: I could be managing the team well in 2035 and still see paid contracts shrink after 2036.
fieldNote: A small **debt payment** stays tied to school costs rather than draining the family reserve.
The future **job search** requires actual post-2036 contract loss, an advertised opening, written pay, hours and date.

steps.text: Keep signed paid returns only while the firm offers them
Pay extra 75 toward mortgage monthly if school costs allow
After 2036 cuts, seek posted compliance job with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The 2028 AGI picture worries me most because the desk work could go before our mortgage can adjust. A written staffing plan and a real paid route into compliance work would help more than reassurance.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what I would miss. I would miss explaining a strange number to a client and watching their shoulders come down.

headlineQuote: I would miss explaining a strange number to a client and watching their shoulders come down.
portrait: Carlos is a **43 year old** senior accountant with a master’s degree and chartered qualification who values explaining errors to clients.
He uses **AI daily**, checks original invoices, and asks his manager to see correction counts alongside time saved.
His partner’s shifts, two school children, mortgage and **three month reserve** keep his plans tied to actual wages.
He tests tools with permission, builds tax dispute skills conditionally, and seeks **written job offers** before leaving paid work.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture threatens his desk income before his mortgage and three month reserve can adjust.
whatWouldHelp: A **written staffing plan** and a real paid route into compliance work would help him.
